nahhas-irab:1-2.t: يُسَبِّحُ may refer to the future and the present. الْمَلِكِ الْقُدُّوسِ الْعَزِيزِ الْحَكِيمِ: naʿt (adjective), and it carries the meaning of praise. The accusative is permissible outside the Qurʾān in the meaning of "I mean"; the nominative is permissible on the basis of an implied mubtadaʾ (subject); and it is permissible without anything implied: you make it nominative as the mubtadaʾ, with الذي as the khabar (predicate). The implied form may be "He is the King, the Holy", with الَّذِي a naʿt of الملك. If you use the genitive, هُوَ is nominative as the mubtadaʾ and الَّذِي is its khabar; and «هو» may be nominative as a tawkīd (emphasis) of what is in الحكيم, with «الذي» a naʿt of الحكيم. بَعَثَ فِي الْأُمِّيِّينَ رَسُولًا مِنْهُمْ is included in the ṣila (relative clause). يَتْلُوا عَلَيْهِمْ is in the position of an accusative, i.e. "reciting to them", a naʿt of رسول. وَيُزَكِّيهِمْ وَيُعَلِّمُهُمُ الْكِتابَ وَالْحِكْمَةَ: the meaning of يزكيهم is that he calls them to obedience to Allah, Mighty and Majestic; when they obey Him they have been purified and he has purified them. وَإِنْ كانُوا مِنْ قَبْلُ لَفِي ضَلالٍ مُبِينٍ: assimilating the lām into the lām is permissible.

nahhas-irab:3-3.t:
وَآخَرِينَ مِنْهُمْ is in the position of a genitive because it is conjoined to الأميين; it may be in the position of an accusative, conjoined to «هم» in يعلّمهم or to «هم» in يزكيهم; and it may be conjoined to the sense of يَتْلُوا عَلَيْهِمْ آياتِهِ, i.e. he makes it known to them. لَمَّا يَلْحَقُوا بِهِمْ: Ibn Zayd said:
i.e. for whoever comes of the Arabs and non-Arabs until the Day of Resurrection; and Mujāhid said: for whoever followed after them, of all people. Abū Jaʿfar said: this is the soundest of what has been said about it, because the verse is general. لمّا is «لم» to which «ما» has been added for emphasis. Sībawayh said: «لمّا» is the answer to whoever says "he has done" (qad faʿala), and «لم» is the answer to whoever says "he did" (faʿala). Abū Jaʿfar said: except that what governs the jussive, according to all, is لم, and for that reason the nūn is dropped. وَهُوَ الْعَزِيزُ الْحَكِيمُ: whoever makes the hāʾ quiescent [Translator's note: i.e. wa-hwa] says: the ḍamma is heavy, and the word has been joined to what precedes it.

nahhas-irab:4-4.t: ذلِكَ فَضْلُ اللَّهِ يُؤْتِيهِ مَنْ يَشاءُ i.e. that which these have been given is a bounty from Allah, Majestic and Mighty, which He gives to whom He wills. وَاللَّهُ ذُو الْفَضْلِ الْعَظِيمِ i.e. He is not blamed for diverting it from whomever He diverts it, because He has not withheld from him a right that he had with Him, nor wronged him by withholding it from him; rather, He knew that someone else was more deserving of it than he, so He diverted it to him.

nahhas-irab:5-5.t: مَثَلُ الَّذِينَ حُمِّلُوا التَّوْراةَ i.e. they were charged with upholding it and stopping at what is in it. ثُمَّ لَمْ يَحْمِلُوها i.e. they did not do that. كَمَثَلِ الْحِمارِ يَحْمِلُ أَسْفاراً: «يحمل» is in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "carrying". If it is said: how is this permissible, when one does not say جاءني غلام هند مسرعة? The answer is that the meaning is "their likeness is the likeness of those who were charged with the Torah" [Translator's note: so in the source]. The Kufans claimed that يحمل is a ṣila of الحمار, because it is in the status of an indefinite, and they call the naʿt of an indefinite a ṣila; then they contradicted this and said: the meaning is "like the likeness of the donkey, carrying books". بِئْسَ مَثَلُ الْقَوْمِ الَّذِينَ كَذَّبُوا بِآياتِ اللَّهِ i.e. "this likeness"; then "this" was omitted because it has already been mentioned. وَاللَّهُ لا يَهْدِي الْقَوْمَ الظَّالِمِينَ: the meaning is that He does not grant them success nor guide them aright, since it was in His knowledge that they would not believe; and it is said: He does not guide them to the reward.

nahhas-irab:6-6.t: قُلْ يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ هادُوا: one says هاد يهود when he repents and when he returns. إِنْ زَعَمْتُمْ أَنَّكُمْ أَوْلِياءُ لِلَّهِ مِنْ دُونِ النَّاسِ i.e. other than you. فَتَمَنَّوُا الْمَوْتَ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ صادِقِينَ i.e. if you are truthful that you are [His] friends — for He does not punish His friends — then wish for it, so that you find rest from the distress of this world, its cares and its griefs, and go on to the repose of Paradise.

nahhas-irab:7-7.t: وَلا يَتَمَنَّوْنَهُ أَبَداً: and it was true, as He, Majestic and Mighty, said, and they refrained from that. بِما قَدَّمَتْ أَيْدِيهِمْ i.e. of sins. وَاللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ بِالظَّالِمِينَ i.e. possessing knowledge of whoever has wronged himself and ruined and destroyed himself through disbelief.

nahhas-irab:8-8.t: قُلْ إِنَّ الْمَوْتَ الَّذِي تَفِرُّونَ مِنْهُ i.e. which you refuse to wish for. الَّذِي is in the position of an accusative, a naʿt (adjective) of الموت. فَإِنَّهُ مُلاقِيكُمْ is the khabar (predicate) of إنّ. The entry of the fāʾ is permissible — whereas إنّ أخاك فمنطلق is not permissible — because the sentence carries the meaning of requital (jazāʾ). The Kufans permitted إنّ ضاربك فظالم, because according to them the sentence carries the meaning of requital. There is another view on it: that الذي تفرون منه is the khabar of إنّ — "death is that from which you flee". ثُمَّ تُرَدُّونَ إِلى عالِمِ الْغَيْبِ وَالشَّهادَةِ: a sentence conjoined to a sentence. فَيُنَبِّئُكُمْ بِما كُنْتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ is conjoined to تردون.

nahhas-irab:9-9.t:
Al-Aʿmash read الْجُمُعَةِ with the mīm quiescent [al-jumʿa], and the dialect of the Banū ʿUqayl is «من يوم الجمعة» with fatḥa on the mīm [al-jumaʿa]. [Translator's note: the print shows al-jumuʿa in both places.] Whoever reads الْجُمُعَةِ [al-jumʿa] explains it in several ways. Among them: the original is al-jumuʿa, and then the ḍamma was dropped because of its heaviness. It may be that this is a dialect with the same meaning as that. And a third answer: it is made quiescent because the assembling takes place in it, so it resembles the object, just as one says رجل هزأة, i.e. one who is laughed at, and لحنة, i.e. one whose speech is corrected. Whoever says الْجُمُعَةِ [al-jumaʿa] attributes the action to it, i.e. it assembles people, just as one says رجل لحنة, i.e. he corrects people's speech, and قراء, i.e. he teaches people to recite. فَاسْعَوْا إِلى ذِكْرِ اللَّهِ: Qatāda said: i.e. with your hearts and your deeds, i.e. proceed. وَذَرُوا الْبَيْعَ: in the past tense one does not say وذر. Sībawayh said: they made do with ترك instead of it; and someone else said: because the wāw is heavy, so they turned to ترك, since it has its meaning. ذلِكُمْ خَيْرٌ لَكُمْ i.e. hastening to the remembrance of Allah. Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab said: and it is the sermon — better for you than buying and selling.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: when the sun passes the meridian, buying and selling become forbidden; and someone else said: the apparent sense of the Qurʾān shows that that is when the muezzin calls the adhān while the imam is on the pulpit. إِنْ كُنْتُمْ تَعْلَمُونَ what holds your benefit and your harm.

nahhas-irab:10-10.t:
I.e. the Friday prayer. فَانْتَشِرُوا فِي الْأَرْضِ i.e. if you wish — what precedes it shows that — and the exegetes said: it is a permission. In the ḥadīth from Anas ibn Mālik, traced back to the Prophet (marfūʿ): فَانْتَشِرُوا فِي الْأَرْضِ وَابْتَغُوا مِنْ فَضْلِ اللَّهِ. Abū Jaʿfar said: for visiting a sick person, or attending a funeral, or visiting, i.e. for the sake of Allah. [Translator's note: the attribution "Abū Jaʿfar said" appears in the source in the middle of the ḥadīth's explanation, as printed.]
The apparent sense of the verse shows the permissibility of dispersing in the land to seek provision in this world or reward in the Hereafter. وَاذْكُرُوا اللَّهَ كَثِيراً i.e. for what [He has bestowed] upon you [Translator's note: the source reads لما عليكم; a verb such as أنعم appears to be missing] and the success He has granted you. لَعَلَّكُمْ تُفْلِحُونَ i.e. you will enter Paradise and abide in it; and al-falāḥ is permanence.

nahhas-irab:11-11.t:
وَإِذا رَأَوْا تِجارَةً أَوْ لَهْواً انْفَضُّوا إِلَيْها: the scholars differed about the "amusement" (al-lahw) here. Sulaymān ibn Bilāl narrated from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad from his father from Jābir, who said: when a woman was given in marriage, the pipes would be played for her and people would rush to it; so Allah, Majestic and Mighty, sent down this. Mujāhid said: the lahw is the drum. Abū Jaʿfar said: the first view is nearer to correctness, because Jābir witnessed the revelation. Al-Farrāʾ inclined to the second view because, according to what he mentioned, when a caravan of trade arrived they would beat a drum for it and people would rush to it; and al-Farrāʾ relied in his book on the meanings [i.e. Maʿānī l-Qurʾān] on al-Kalbī, and al-Kalbī is abandoned in ḥadīth. As for His saying, Majestic and Mighty, انْفَضُّوا إِلَيْها, and He did not say إليهما, its implied form according to the view of Muḥammad ibn Yazīd is "and when they saw trade they dispersed to it"; then the second was conjoined to the first and entered into what it entered into. Al-Farrāʾ claimed that the preferred thing is for the pronoun to refer back to the second; had it been as he said, it would have been انفضوا إليه; but he argues in this that what is intended is the trade. All of this is permissible: that it refer back to the first, or to the second, or to both. He, Majestic and Mighty, said: وَمَنْ يَكْسِبْ خَطِيئَةً أَوْ إِثْماً ثُمَّ يَرْمِ بِهِ بَرِيئاً
[al-Nisāʾ: 112], where the pronoun refers back to the second; and He, Majestic and Mighty, said: إِنْ يَكُنْ غَنِيًّا أَوْ فَقِيراً فَاللَّهُ أَوْلى بِهِما [al-Nisāʾ: 135], where it refers back to both of them together. وَتَرَكُوكَ قائِماً: accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. standing delivering the sermon. قُلْ ما عِنْدَ اللَّهِ خَيْرٌ مِنَ اللَّهْوِ وَمِنَ التِّجارَةِ i.e. what He has of reward.
وَاللَّهُ خَيْرُ الرَّازِقِينَ i.e. so ask Him alone, and turn in longing to Him alone, that He may give you ample provision.
